descriptors.concept_name: Provisions to Counteract Unethical Tax Practices Overview
descriptors.definition: The Income-tax Act provides penal provisions and prosecution tools to handle defaults, deter tax avoidance, and combat unlawful tax practices. Penalties are imposed by tax authorities, whereas fines and criminal prosecutions are initiated through a court Magistrate.
instrument_references: Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015
inclusion: penalties for default under the Income-tax Act
prosecution provisions enforced via Courts
taxation of undisclosed foreign income
exclusion: civil assessment procedures unconnected to default
nearby_distinctions: Penalties are levied by departmental tax authorities, whereas fines and prosecution sentences are administered exclusively by a judicial Magistrate.

descriptors.concept_name: Penal Provisions Under The Income Tax Act
descriptors.definition: Penalties are distinct from regular tax or interest and are assessed based on the law active when a default occurred. Competent authorities hold discretionary power to levy penalties within statutory minimum and maximum limits.
inclusion: penalties levied over and above tax and interest
discretionary powers of commissioners to reduce or waive penalties
exclusion: tax and interest amounts payable under regular assessment
penalties governed by laws enacted after the default date
nearby_distinctions: Penalties apply specifically to statutory non-compliance or under-reporting, differing fundamentally from the principal tax liability.

descriptors.concept_name: Penalty Leviable For Under Reporting Of Income [Section 270A]
descriptors.definition: Section 270A imposes monetary penalties where an assessee underreports income, determined by comparing assessed income against processed return figures or basic exemption thresholds. Specified higher authorities are empowered to issue written penalty orders during ongoing assessment proceedings.
inclusion: penalties on income under-reporting during regular assessments and reassessments
adjustments involving MAT and AMT provisions
exclusion: concealment penalties under legacy section 271 for assessment years from A.Y. 2017-18 onward
nearby_distinctions: Section 270A replaces older concealment rules to provide structured certainty based on mathematical comparisons between returned and assessed incomes.

descriptors.concept_name: Other Penal Provisions Under The Income Tax Act
descriptors.definition: Chapter XXI contains specific penalties triggered when taxpayers fail to maintain books of accounts, retain transfer pricing documentation, or comply with search-related disclosures. These specific provisions operate alongside general under-reporting rules subject to statutory exclusions.
inclusion: penalties for failing to keep required books or transfer pricing records
penalties for undisclosed income discovered during searches
exclusion: general under-reporting penalties under section 270A where specific search penalties already apply to the same undisclosed income
nearby_distinctions: These target procedural defaults and specialized compliance failures rather than general computational understatements of income.

descriptors.concept_name: Taxation Of Undisclosed Sources Of Income
descriptors.definition: Unexplained financial items such as cash credits, unverified investments, and undisclosed expenditures are treated as taxable income when the assessee fails to provide a satisfactory explanation. For loans or share capital in closely held companies, additional validation from the creditor or shareholder is mandatory.
inclusion: unexplained cash credits and hundi borrowings
unexplained share application money and share premium in closely held companies
unaccounted investments and expenditures
exclusion: share capital credits where the investor is a SEBI-registered Venture Capital Fund or Company
credits where satisfactory explanations of nature and source are provided
nearby_distinctions: Unlike normal business receipts, these provisions shift the burden entirely onto the assessee to prove the legitimate source of unrecorded entries.

descriptors.concept_name: Penalty Not Leviable In Certain Cases [Section 273B]
descriptors.definition: Section 273B protects assessees from statutory penalties for specific procedural and reporting failures if they establish a reasonable cause for the default. This waiver applies across a designated list of penalty provisions under the Act.
inclusion: exemptions from penalties upon proving a valid, reasonable cause for non-compliance
exclusion: penalties where no statutory reference to reasonable cause is provided under Section 273B
nearby_distinctions: Section 273B provides a blanket exculpatory defense based on reasonable cause, distinct from discretionary reductions by commissioners.

descriptors.definition: Penalty imposition requires granting the assessee a reasonable opportunity of being heard and, where penalty amounts exceed specified monetary thresholds, obtaining prior approval from a Joint Commissioner. The Central Government is empowered to formulate faceless penalty schemes to optimize administrative resources.
inclusion: mandates for giving a hearing opportunity before imposing penalties
hierarchical approval thresholds for Income-tax Officers and Assistant Commissioners
faceless penalty scheme implementation
exclusion: penalty orders passed without observing principles of natural justice or required administrative clearances
nearby_distinctions: Procedural safeguards under Section 274 regulate the administrative execution of penalties rather than their substantive computation.

descriptors.concept_name: Time Limit For Imposition Of Penalty [Section 275]
descriptors.definition: Section 275 establishes strict statutory time limits for passing penalty orders based on whether the underlying assessment is subjected to appeals, revisions, or standard closure. These limits typically tie the final penalty order date to the completion of assessment proceedings or the receipt of appellate orders.
inclusion: deadlines for penalty orders following tribunal or commissioner appeals
time constraints linked to revision proceedings
exclusion: unbounded or delayed penalty orders exceeding statutory expiry windows
nearby_distinctions: Time limits under Section 275 strictly govern when a penalty order can be issued post-assessment, differing from assessment time bars.

descriptors.concept_name: Offences And Prosecution Under The Income Tax Act
descriptors.definition: Chapter XXII prescribes rigorous imprisonment and fines for serious tax offenses, including search obstructions, tax evasion, and failure to credit deducted or collected taxes. Specific monetary thresholds and timelines govern the severity of imprisonment terms.
inclusion: criminal prosecutions and imprisonment for tax and TDS evasion
penalties for failing to surrender assets or obstruct search actions
exclusion: purely civil monetary penalties imposed departmentally without criminal intent
nearby_distinctions: Prosecution involves criminal court trials and imprisonment, whereas penalties are administrative monetary sanctions.

descriptors.concept_name: Presumption As To Culpable Mental State [Section 278E]
descriptors.definition: In any prosecution requiring a culpable mental state, courts must legally presume the existence of such intent, shifting the burden of proof onto the accused. The accused must prove the complete absence of a guilty mind beyond a reasonable doubt to successfully defend against the charge.
inclusion: mandatory court presumptions of intent in prosecution cases
statutory placement of the burden of proof on the accused
exclusion: civil penalty proceedings where the revenue department retains the burden of proof for concealment
nearby_distinctions: Section 278E explicitly reverses the ordinary burden of proof for criminal tax offenses by presuming mens rea until rebutted by the accused.

descriptors.concept_name: Prosecution To Be Made At The Instance Of The Principal Chief Commissioner Or Chief Commissioner Or Principal Commissioner Or Commissioner [Sections 279 And 279A]
descriptors.definition: Initiating prosecution proceedings requires prior written sanction from designated senior income-tax authorities. Statutes also permit the compounding of offenses and ensure statements made during assessment proceedings remain admissible as evidence.
inclusion: prior sanction requirements for criminal proceedings
legal provisions for compounding tax offenses
admissibility of prior statements in court
exclusion: prosecutions launched directly by junior assessing officers without higher sanction
nearby_distinctions: Sanction rules act as a filtering administrative check before criminal courts take cognizance of tax offenses.

descriptors.concept_name: Immunity From Imposition Of Penalty And Prosecution [Section 270AA]
descriptors.definition: Assessees can apply for immunity from under-reporting penalties and related prosecutions if they pay assessed taxes and interest within the demand period and refrain from filing appeals. Immunity is restricted and cannot be granted if assessments involve severe infractions like misrepresentation or unrecorded entries.
inclusion: applications for penalty and prosecution immunity upon paying due taxes
statutory bars against granting immunity for suppression or false entries
exclusion: cases where the assessee pursues appellate litigation against the assessment order
nearby_distinctions: Immunity under Section 270AA requires immediate tax compliance and forfeiture of appeal rights, unlike regular appellate dispute resolution.
